newsitem.title: UK: Russia dollar Eurobond seen for 10 years - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Russia dollar Eurobond seen for 10 years - bankers.

text.p: Russia's forthcoming dollar Eurobond is expected to have a 10-year maturity, reflecting strong demand for the country's assets, bankers said on Thursday.
"Russia is planning a seven- or 10-year maturity," an Eastern European analyst at a U.S. investment bank said.
"If they can get away with a 10-year bond they will do it, and the market is looking good enough to do so at the moment," he said.
Roadshows for the deal, expected to be for $1.0 billion, are now under way and will be completed on June 18. Launch is expected shortly after.
The bond will be underwritten by J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg. Officials there were not available for comment.
In May, Russian officials said the maturity of the June deal would be around seven years with subsequent issues extending its borrowing tenor to 10 or 20 years.

But bankers said the strong performance of recent debut Eurobonds launched by the cities of Moscow and St Petersburg showed demand for Russian paper was strong, and investors could offer Russia money for a longer term.
Moscow raised $500 million via a three-year bond, launched to yield 315 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. On Thursday the paper traded at 278 b.p. over.
St Petersburg launched a $300 million five-year bond last week at 312.5 b.p. over, which by Thursday was trading at a 304 b.p. spread.
"There is very, very bullish sentiment towards Eastern European credits, although it hasn't extended towards the corporate sector yet," a syndicate manager involved in Russian transactions said.
"For sovereigns, big cities and credits close to the sovereign, there is a lot of demand," he said.
Spread talk on a 10-year Russian bond ranged between 350 to 375 b.p. over Treasuries to 370 to 395 b.p. over.
"At current market conditions, we expect Russia to be priced at around 375 b.p. over," a dealer at a European bank said.

Russia first tapped the international capital markets in November 1996, when it launched a $1.0 billion five-year bond at 345 b.p. over Treasuries. The bond was trading at around 275 b.p. over on Thursday, although the spread has had a volatile history, widening after launch.
In March Russia raised 2.0 billion marks via a seven-year bond which was trading at around 347 b.p. over Bunds on Thursday, down from a 370 b.p. launch spread.
"Following the superb performance of Moscow and St Petersburg, investors bought into Russia's outstanding debt and these deals tightened too," a trader said.
"Investors are keen to get into new deals because they expect them to perform well," he said.
Another debt dealer said: "The first Russian dollar bond was difficult, and the spread quite volatile. The mark bond was launched into a difficult market."
"Investors still want to see the Russian Federation perform, and they also know it will borrow substantial amounts in the future. Moscow and St Petersburg had more rarity appeal," he said.
Russia is expected to launch a dollar global bond in the Autumn. Russian 1998 budget plans foresee $3.0 billion in Eurobond issues next year.
-- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
